title: The zero locus of an etale section is Zariski open
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with abelian sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $p:V\to T$ be an etale object with $s\in F(V)$. There is a largest Zariski open subset $W\subseteq V$ on which $s$ restricts to zero. For every morphism $h:V'\to V$ in $T_{\Et}$, $s|_{V'}=0$ if and only if $h(V')\subseteq W$. For every geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, the germ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] of $s$ in $F_{p\bar v}$ is zero if and only if the underlying point of $\bar v$ belongs to $W$.

source.place: Tag 04FR, lemma-zero-over-image, clauses (1)-(3); support complement as in Tag 04FT, lemma-support-section-closed (1)

proof.text: Apply the existing agreement-open theorem to the underlying sheaf of sets of F, with the second section the zero section. It supplies an étale object W and an open E with restriction equality equivalent to range containment.

Use the underlying function of the additive-group restriction map and the fact that equality with the zero section is equivalent to being zero. Identify the open E with the étale object W and use the open immersion range formula to obtain the first two clauses.

For the geometric-stalk clause, use the filtered-colimit equality criterion to represent a zero germ by a pointed étale refinement whose restriction is zero. The agreement criterion places the image of that refinement in W, and the open-immersion lifting property gives the required factorization through W. Conversely, a factorization through W gives a pointed lift; the agreement criterion makes the restriction zero, and toPresheafFiber_w transports this zero to the original germ.
